people.name: Robert Bruce Foote
people.summary: Geologist who found India's first Palaeolithic hand-axe at Pallavaram near Madras (1863); "father of Indian prehistory".
facts: Found the Pallavaram hand-axe (1863).
Explored many prehistoric sites in Andhra, including the Kurnool caves (Billa Surgam).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Alexander Cunningham
people.summary: First Director-General of the Archaeological Survey of India, "father of Indian archaeology"; reported a Harappan seal in 1875 without realising its age (NCERT).
facts: First Director-General of the ASI (1861) (NCERT).
Reported a Harappan seal (1875) (NCERT).
Used Xuanzang's accounts to locate early Buddhist sites (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 1 "Bricks, Beads and Bones"

people.name: Daya Ram Sahni
people.summary: Archaeologist who began excavations at Harappa in 1921 (NCERT); later the first Indian Director-General of the ASI.
facts: Found seals at Harappa in layers much older than early historic levels (NCERT).
First Indian Director-General of the ASI (1931).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 1 "Bricks, Beads and Bones"

people.name: Rakhal Das Banerji
people.summary: Archaeologist who found Harappan seals at Mohenjodaro (excavations from 1922) (NCERT).
facts: Found similar seals at Mohenjodaro (NCERT).
Wrote on the Palas and on Bengali history.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 1 "Bricks, Beads and Bones"

people.name: John Marshall
people.summary: Director-General of the ASI who announced the discovery of a new civilisation in the Indus valley in 1924 (NCERT).
facts: Announced the Indus civilisation to the world (1924) (NCERT).
Dug in horizontal units ignoring stratigraphy (NCERT).
Also excavated Taxila and restored Sanchi.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 1 "Bricks, Beads and Bones"

people.name: Mortimer Wheeler
people.summary: Director-General of the ASI from 1944 who corrected the excavation method by following stratigraphy (NCERT).
facts: Took over the ASI in 1944 (NCERT).
Proposed an "Aryan invasion" massacre at Mohenjodaro, later disproved by G.F. Dales (1964) (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 1 "Bricks, Beads and Bones"

people.name: Vardhamana Mahavira
people.summary: Twenty-fourth and last tirthankara of the Jainas; preached non-violence (ahimsa) in Magadha and around (NCERT).
facts: Born at Kundagrama near Vaishali to a Kshatriya family of the Jnatrika clan.
Left home at 30; attained kevala jnana (supreme knowledge) at 42.
Gave five vows: ahimsa, satya, asteya, aparigraha, brahmacharya (the last added by him).
Died at Pavapuri near Rajagriha.
The Jainas say 23 tirthankaras came before him; Parshvanatha was the 23rd (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 4 "Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings"

people.name: Gautama Buddha
people.summary: Founder of Buddhism; a Shakya prince, Siddhartha, who attained enlightenment at Bodh Gaya and taught the Middle Path (NCERT).
facts: Born at Lumbini (Nepal) to the Shakya chief Suddhodana and Maya.
Left home after seeing an old man, a sick man, a corpse and an ascetic (NCERT).
Enlightened under a peepal tree at Bodh Gaya (NCERT).
First sermon at Sarnath (Dhammachakkapavattana).
Died (mahaparinibbana) at Kusinagara (NCERT).
Taught the Four Noble Truths and the Eightfold Path.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 4 "Thinkers, Beliefs and Buildings"

people.name: Bimbisara
people.summary: Haryanka king of Magadha who expanded it through marriage alliances and the conquest of Anga; a patron of the Buddha.
facts: Married princesses of Kosala, Vaishali (Lichchhavi) and Madra.
Conquered Anga; capital Rajagriha.
Sent his physician Jivaka to Avanti.
Imprisoned and killed by his son Ajatashatru.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Ajatashatru
people.summary: Haryanka king of Magadha who killed his father Bimbisara, defeated Kosala and the Vajji confederacy, and hosted the First Buddhist Council.
facts: Used catapults (mahashilakantaka) and chariots with maces (rathamusala) against the Vajjis.
Fortified Pataligrama, later Pataliputra.
Patron of the First Buddhist Council at Rajagriha.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Photo Dharma from Penang, Malaysia / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Mahapadma Nanda
people.summary: Founder of the Nanda dynasty of Magadha, called "ekarat" (sole sovereign) and "destroyer of all Kshatriyas".
facts: Overthrew the Shishunagas (c. 345 BCE).
Conquered Kalinga; Kharavela's inscription says a Nanda king built a canal there.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Jean-Michel Moullec from Vern sur Seiche (35, Bretagne), France / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Dhana Nanda
people.summary: Last Nanda king, whose huge army deterred Alexander's soldiers; overthrown by Chandragupta Maurya and Chanakya.
facts: Greek writers call him Agrammes or Xandrames.
Unpopular for heavy taxes.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Alexander of Macedon
people.summary: Macedonian conqueror who invaded north-west India (327–325 BCE) (NCERT) and defeated Porus at the Hydaspes (326 BCE).
facts: Crossed the Hindu Kush (327 BCE); welcomed by Ambhi of Taxila.
Defeated Porus at the Jhelum (Hydaspes) (326 BCE).
His army refused to go beyond the Beas (Hyphasis).
Died at Babylon (323 BCE).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 2 "Kings, Farmers and Towns"

people.name: Porus
people.summary: King of the land between the Jhelum and the Chenab who fought Alexander at the Hydaspes (326 BCE) and was restored as a subordinate ruler.
facts: Asked how he wished to be treated, he is said to have replied "as a king".
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Chandragupta Maurya
people.summary: Founder of the Mauryan empire (c. 321 BCE) (NCERT), who overthrew the Nandas with Chanakya and defeated Seleucus.
facts: Accession c. 321 BCE (NCERT).
Extended control as far north-west as Afghanistan and Baluchistan (NCERT).
Treaty with Seleucus Nicator (c. 305 BCE); Megasthenes came to his court.
Became a Jaina; went with Bhadrabahu to Shravanabelagola, Karnataka, and died by sallekhana.

roles.title: Mauryan emperor
roles.howGained: Overthrew Dhana Nanda with Chanakya's help
roles.howEnded: Abdicated and became a Jaina monk

people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 2 "Kings, Farmers and Towns"

people.name: Chanakya
people.summary: Brahmana minister of Chandragupta Maurya, traditionally the author of the Arthashastra (NCERT).
facts: Also called Kautilya and Vishnugupta.
The Arthashastra, a treatise on statecraft, is traditionally ascribed to him (NCERT).
Taught at Taxila, by tradition.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 2 "Kings, Farmers and Towns"

people.name: Seleucus Nicator
people.summary: Alexander's general who ruled the eastern provinces; lost to Chandragupta Maurya and ceded territory for 500 elephants (c. 305 BCE).
facts: Ceded Arachosia, Gedrosia, Paropamisadae (and Aria) to Chandragupta.
Sent Megasthenes as ambassador.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Megasthenes
people.summary: Greek ambassador of Seleucus at Chandragupta's court in Pataliputra; wrote the Indica (NCERT).
facts: His account of Pataliputra and the army survives in quotations (NCERT).
Described seven "castes" of Indian society.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 2 "Kings, Farmers and Towns"

people.name: Bhadrabahu
people.summary: Jaina teacher who led monks south to Karnataka during a famine, taking Chandragupta Maurya with him.
facts: Died at Shravanabelagola.
His migration led later to the Digambara–Shvetambara split.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Bindusara
people.summary: Second Mauryan emperor, son of Chandragupta; the Greeks called him Amitrochates ("slayer of foes").
facts: Asked Antiochus I for sweet wine, dried figs and a philosopher.
Patron of the Ajivika sect.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Photo Dharma from Penang, Malaysia / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Ashoka
people.summary: Third Mauryan emperor (c. 272/268–231 BCE) (NCERT), who conquered Kalinga, turned to Buddhism and spread dhamma through inscriptions on rocks and pillars (NCERT).
facts: Called "Devanampiya Piyadassi" (beloved of the gods, of pleasing appearance) in his inscriptions (NCERT).
Conquered Kalinga (c. 261 BCE) (NCERT).
Appointed dhamma mahamattas to spread dhamma (NCERT).
His Brahmi inscriptions were deciphered by James Prinsep (1838) (NCERT).
Sent his son Mahinda and daughter Sanghamitta to Sri Lanka.
The Sarnath lion capital is India's national emblem.

roles.title: Mauryan emperor
roles.howGained: Won a succession struggle; crowned about four years later

people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 2 "Kings, Farmers and Towns"

people.name: Mahinda
people.summary: Ashoka's son who took Buddhism to Sri Lanka.
facts: Converted King Devanampiya Tissa of Sri Lanka.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Sanghamitta
people.summary: Ashoka's daughter who took a sapling of the Bodhi tree to Sri Lanka and founded the order of nuns there.
facts: Planted the Bodhi sapling at Anuradhapura.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Moggaliputta Tissa
people.summary: Monk who presided over the Third Buddhist Council at Pataliputra under Ashoka.
facts: Compiled the Kathavatthu.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: Photo Dharma from Penang, Malaysia / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: James Prinsep
people.summary: Official of the East India Company mint who deciphered Ashokan Brahmi and Kharosthi (1838) (NCERT).
facts: Deciphered Brahmi in 1838, after decades of work by epigraphists (NCERT).
Found that "Piyadassi" was Ashoka.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 2 "Kings, Farmers and Towns"

people.name: Mahakassapa
people.summary: Senior disciple of the Buddha who presided over the First Buddhist Council at Rajagriha.
facts: Presided over the First Council soon after the Buddha's death.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Simuka
people.summary: Founder of the Satavahana dynasty of the Deccan (c. 230 BCE).
facts: Named first in the Satavahana list in the Puranas and at Naneghat.
The Puranas call the dynasty "Andhra-bhrityas".

roles.title: Satavahana king
roles.howGained: Founded the dynasty after Mauryan decline

people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Pushyamitra Shunga
people.summary: Brahmana general who killed the last Maurya, Brihadratha (c. 185 BCE), founded the Shunga dynasty and performed two ashvamedhas.
facts: Fought the Indo-Greeks.
Patanjali, author of the Mahabhashya, is said to have been his priest.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Patanjali
people.summary: Grammarian of the Shunga age who wrote the Mahabhashya on Panini's grammar; the Yoga Sutras are also ascribed to a Patanjali.
facts: Mahabhashya: commentary on Panini's Ashtadhyayi.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Menander
people.summary: Most famous Indo-Greek king, ruling from Sakala (Sialkot); his dialogue with the monk Nagasena is recorded in the Milindapanha.
facts: Became a Buddhist, by tradition.
Indo-Greeks were the first to issue coins with kings' portraits and names.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Kharavela
people.summary: Jaina king of Kalinga (Chedi dynasty) whose Hathigumpha inscription at Udayagiri records his campaigns year by year.
facts: Hathigumpha inscription near Bhubaneswar.
Claims to have defeated a Satavahana king and the king of Magadha.
Patron of Jainism.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Kanishka
people.summary: Greatest Kushana king, patron of Mahayana Buddhism and the Fourth Buddhist Council; his accession (78 CE) is linked to the Saka era (NCERT dates the Kushanas c. 1st century CE).
facts: Capital at Purushapura (Peshawar); second capital Mathura.
Convened the Fourth Buddhist Council in Kashmir (Kundalavana).
Kushana kings called themselves devaputra (son of god) (NCERT).
Patron of Ashvaghosha, Vasumitra, Nagarjuna (by tradition) and Charaka.
Gandhara and Mathura schools of art flourished.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 2 "Kings, Farmers and Towns"

images.credit: No machine-readable author provided. World Imaging assumed (based on copyright claims). / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Ashvaghosha
people.summary: Buddhist poet at Kanishka's court who wrote the Buddhacharita in Sanskrit.
facts: Wrote the Buddhacharita and Saundarananda.
Vice-president of the Fourth Buddhist Council, by tradition.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Acharya Nagarjuna
people.summary: Mahayana philosopher of the Madhyamika ("middle way") school, linked by tradition to Nagarjunakonda and the Satavahana court.
facts: Founded the Madhyamika school; taught shunyata (emptiness).
Wrote the Mulamadhyamakakarika.
Called the "Einstein of India" in some textbooks.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Gautamiputra Satakarni
people.summary: Greatest Satavahana king, who defeated the Shaka ruler Nahapana; his mother Gautami Balashri's Nasik inscription praises him (NCERT).
facts: Called "ekabrahmana" (unique brahmana) and destroyer of the Shakas, Yavanas and Pahlavas (Nasik inscription) (NCERT).
Satavahana kings were known by metronymics — names from their mothers (NCERT).
Restruck Nahapana's coins.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 2 "Kings, Farmers and Towns"

people.name: Vasishthiputra Pulumavi
people.summary: Satavahana king who succeeded Gautamiputra and shifted the centre east to Andhra, with capital Dhanyakataka (Amaravati).
facts: Inscriptions at Amaravati.
Rudradaman defeated a Satavahana king — possibly his successor.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Hala
people.summary: Satavahana king and poet who compiled the Gathasaptashati, 700 Prakrit verses.
facts: Gathasaptashati (Gaha Sattasai) in Maharashtri Prakrit.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Rudradaman I
people.summary: Shaka (Western Kshatrapa) ruler of Ujjain whose Junagadh inscription (c. 150 CE) is the first long inscription in Sanskrit (NCERT).
facts: Repaired the Sudarshana lake, built under Chandragupta Maurya and improved under Ashoka (NCERT).
Claims to have defeated the Satavahana king twice.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 2 "Kings, Farmers and Towns"

people.name: Karikala
people.summary: Greatest early Chola king, who won at Venni and built the Kallanai dam on the Kaveri (by tradition); capital Uraiyur, port Puhar.
facts: Victory at Venni over the Cheras and Pandyas.
Credited with the Kallanai (Grand Anicut).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Vasishthiputra Chamtamula
people.summary: Founder of the Ikshvaku dynasty of the Krishna valley, with capital Vijayapuri (Nagarjunakonda); performed Vedic sacrifices.
facts: Performed the ashvamedha and vajapeya.
His sister and queens patronised Buddhism at Nagarjunakonda.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Chandragupta I
people.summary: First great Gupta king (from c. 320 CE), who married the Lichchhavi princess Kumaradevi and took the title Maharajadhiraja.
facts: The Gupta era begins in 319–320 CE.
Gold coins show him with Kumaradevi.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Samudragupta
people.summary: Gupta emperor whose conquests are described in Harisena's Prayaga prashasti on the Allahabad pillar (NCERT).
facts: Prayaga prashasti by his court poet Harisena (NCERT).
Uprooted kings of Aryavarta; captured and released twelve kings of Dakshinapatha.
Coins show him playing the veena.
Called the "Napoleon of India" by V.A. Smith.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 2 "Kings, Farmers and Towns"

people.name: Harisena
people.summary: Court poet of Samudragupta who composed the Prayaga prashasti on the Allahabad pillar (NCERT).
facts: Wrote the prashasti in Sanskrit (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 2 "Kings, Farmers and Towns"

people.name: Chandragupta II
people.summary: Gupta emperor (c. 375–415 CE) (NCERT) who defeated the Shakas, took the title Vikramaditya, and at whose court Kalidasa is said to have lived.
facts: Ended Shaka rule in western India; issued silver coins.
Married his daughter Prabhavati to the Vakataka king.
Fa-Hien visited India in his reign.
Mehrauli iron pillar is linked with a king "Chandra".
Navaratnas (nine gems) at his court, by tradition.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 2 "Kings, Farmers and Towns"

people.name: Kalidasa
people.summary: Greatest Sanskrit poet and dramatist, traditionally at the court of Chandragupta II; wrote Abhijnanashakuntalam and Meghaduta.
facts: Plays: Abhijnanashakuntalam, Malavikagnimitram, Vikramorvashiyam.
Poems: Meghaduta, Raghuvamsha, Kumarasambhava, Ritusamhara.
In his plays, kings and brahmanas speak Sanskrit, others Prakrit (NCERT).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Fa-Hien
people.summary: Chinese Buddhist monk who visited India (c. 399–414 CE) during Chandragupta II's reign.
facts: Wrote Records of the Buddhist Kingdoms (Foguoji).
Described Pataliputra and the treatment of "untouchables" who lived outside the town.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Kumaragupta I
people.summary: Gupta emperor (c. 415–455 CE) who founded the monastery-university at Nalanda.
facts: Performed the ashvamedha.
Founded Nalanda (Mahendraditya).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Skandagupta
people.summary: Last great Gupta emperor, who repulsed the Huna invasion; his Junagadh inscription records repairs to the Sudarshana lake.
facts: Defeated the Hunas (c. 455–460 CE).
Repaired the Sudarshana lake again.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Aryabhata
people.summary: Mathematician-astronomer who wrote the Aryabhatiya (499 CE): the earth rotates on its axis, and eclipses are caused by shadows (NCERT).
facts: Wrote the Aryabhatiya at Kusumapura (Pataliputra) at age 23.
Gave a value of pi close to 3.1416 and explained eclipses scientifically (NCERT).
India's first satellite (1975) was named after him.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Harishena
people.summary: Vakataka king in whose time many of the Ajanta caves (16, 17) were cut and painted.
facts: Patron of Ajanta through his minister Varahadeva.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Madhava Varma I
people.summary: Vishnukundin king who made the dynasty powerful in coastal Andhra and Telangana; performed many ashvamedhas.
facts: The Vishnukundins worshipped Sri Parvata Swami (Srisailam).
Capitals at Indrapalanagara and later Denduluru/Amarapura.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Mihirakula
people.summary: Huna king, son of Toramana, known for cruelty to Buddhists; defeated by Yashodharman of Malwa (c. 528 CE).
facts: Xuanzang describes his persecution of Buddhists.
Gwalior inscription.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

images.credit: CNG coins. Contoured by me पाटलिपुत्र (talk) / Wikimedia Commons

people.name: Yashodharman
people.summary: King of Malwa who defeated the Huna Mihirakula (c. 528 CE), as his Mandsaur pillar says.
facts: Mandsaur inscriptions.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Pulakeshin I
people.summary: Founder of the Chalukya dynasty of Badami (Vatapi) (c. 543 CE); performed the ashvamedha.
facts: Fortified Vatapi (Badami).
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Pulakeshin II
people.summary: Greatest Chalukya king of Badami; stopped Harsha at the Narmada (NCERT, Aihole inscription) and was killed when the Pallava Narasimhavarman I took Vatapi (642 CE).
facts: His court poet Ravikirti wrote the Aihole inscription (634 CE) (NCERT).
Conquered Vengi and placed his brother Kubja Vishnuvardhana there (624 CE).
Sent an embassy to Khusrau II of Persia (Ajanta painting, traditionally).
Xuanzang visited his kingdom.

roles.title: Chalukya king of Badami
roles.howGained: Won a civil war against his uncle
roles.howEnded: Killed when Narasimhavarman I took Vatapi

people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 2 "Kings, Farmers and Towns"

people.name: Ravikirti
people.summary: Jaina court poet of Pulakeshin II who wrote the Aihole inscription (634 CE) (NCERT).
facts: Compared himself to Kalidasa and Bharavi in the inscription.
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 2 "Kings, Farmers and Towns"

people.name: Harshavardhana
people.summary: Pushyabhuti king of Thanesar and Kanauj (606–647 CE) (NCERT), patron of Xuanzang and Banabhatta, defeated by Pulakeshin II at the Narmada.
facts: Became king after his brother Rajyavardhana was killed (606 CE).
Moved his capital to Kanauj.
Banabhatta wrote his biography, the Harshacharita (NCERT).
Wrote three plays: Ratnavali, Nagananda and Priyadarshika.
Held assemblies at Kanauj and Prayaga (643 CE).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 2 "Kings, Farmers and Towns"

people.name: Banabhatta
people.summary: Court poet of Harsha who wrote the Harshacharita (NCERT) and the prose romance Kadambari.
facts: Harshacharita is a biography of Harsha in Sanskrit (NCERT).
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 2 "Kings, Farmers and Towns"

people.name: Xuanzang
people.summary: Chinese Buddhist pilgrim who came to India (c. 629–645 CE) in search of Buddhist texts (NCERT), studied at Nalanda and wrote the Si-yu-ki.
facts: Stayed at Nalanda, studying under Shilabhadra.
Attended Harsha's assemblies at Kanauj and Prayaga.
Visited Pulakeshin II's kingdom and Andhra (Dhanyakataka).
Called the "Prince of Pilgrims".
people.source: NCERT Class 12 Themes in Indian History I, Ch. 2 "Kings, Farmers and Towns"

people.name: Kubja Vishnuvardhana
people.summary: Brother of Pulakeshin II who founded the Eastern Chalukya dynasty of Vengi (624 CE).
facts: Ruled from Pishtapura (Pithapuram), later Vengi.
The Eastern Chalukyas ruled coastal Andhra for about 450 years.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Mahendravarman I
people.summary: Pallava king of Kanchi, a poet (Mattavilasa Prahasana), builder of rock-cut temples, converted from Jainism to Shaivism by Appar.
facts: Lost territory to Pulakeshin II.
Called "Vichitrachitta".
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)

people.name: Narasimhavarman I
people.summary: Pallava king who defeated and killed Pulakeshin II and took Vatapi (642 CE), taking the title "Vatapikonda"; built the Mamallapuram rathas.
facts: Called Mamalla (great wrestler).
Xuanzang visited Kanchi in his reign.
people.source: Standard modern Indian history (Spectrum / Bipan Chandra)
